The schema has no fact type connecting Transactions1k to Gasstation, Product, or Customer -- Transactions1kGasStationID/Transactions1kProductID/Transactions1kCustomerID are separate, unlinked value types from GasstationID/ProductID/CustomerID (only Yearmonth has an entity-to-entity link, to Customer). Confirmed with ./try: 'is of'/'has' from Gasstation or Transactions1k toward the other type resolves to no fact type ('no fact type reads is of starting from Gasstation and reaching Transactions1k'; 'has' from Transactions1k is ambiguous ... and none of them reaches Gasstation/Product/Customer). Likely because the underlying SQLite schema lacks FK constraints on transactions_1k, so reverse-engineering left these as plain attributes rather than entity references.

answer: THE DISTINCT COUNT OF cust IN Customer cust [has CustomerCurrency: 'EUR'] is of Yearmonth has YearmonthConsumption c WHERE c > 1000

note: The evidence's 'total consumption per year / number of customers with lowest consumption' always mathematically reduces to just MIN(YearmonthConsumption) for the segment (since averaging a set of tied-minimum values returns that value), so each segment's figure is expressible individually, e.g. THE MINIMUM c IN Customer [has CustomerSegment: 'SME'] [has CustomerCurrency: 'CZK'] is of Yearmonth [has YearmonthDate d] has YearmonthConsumption c WHERE starts_with(d, '2013') (tested: SME=-14896.12, LAM=-2458.05, KAM=-582092.86). But the question wants three differences (SME-LAM, LAM-KAM, KAM-SME) returned together, and ConQuer has no way to combine three independently-computed whole-query aggregates into one result: LIST requires a single FROM path to produce columns, bare aggregate arithmetic produces only one scalar (confirmed two aggregates joined by ',' or 'OR OTHERWISE' both fail to parse/compile), and there is no multi-statement (semicolon) support. No single query returns exactly what was asked.
